claims.text: A molybdenum interlayer between W and CuCrZr will reduce thermal-expansion mismatch.
A molybdenum interlayer will act as a diffusion barrier between W and CuCrZr.
The molybdenum interlayer will enhance interfacial bonding and durability under high-temperature cyclic conditions.
The initial materials are W and CuCrZr in their as-fabricated states.
The intervention is deposition of a thin molybdenum film between W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those relevant to the W/CuCrZr joint.
The intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient of molybdenum mediates thermal stresses.
The molybdenum layer limits interdiffusion during cyclic thermal loading.
Limiting interdiffusion reduces the formation of brittle intermetallic phases at the interface.
Compared with direct W/CuCrZr bonding, the molybdenum interlayer will reduce residual stresses.
Compared with direct W/CuCrZr bonding, the molybdenum interlayer will minimize brittle-phase formation.
Compared with direct W/CuCrZr bonding, the molybdenum interlayer will provide more durable and reliable interfacial bonding.
The benefit of the molybdenum interlayer may depend on its thickness and deposition quality.
Excessively thick or non-uniform molybdenum layers may negate the expected advantages through inadequate diffusion-barrier performance.
The magnitude of stress reduction and bonding-strength improvement may vary with processing conditions and requires experimental validation.
